cards.title: BQL Data Handling in Maximum Likelihood Models
cards.claim: Phoenix handles Below Quantification Limit (BQL) data by using maximum likelihood estimation with censored data. When BQL is enabled, the engine reverts to the Laplacian method. Censored observations (CObsBQL != 0) use the cumulative distribution function for likelihood calculation, while non-censored values use the probability density function.
conditions: BQL option must be selected in the model configuration.
Data must include a column flagging censored vs. non-censored values (e.g., CObsBQL).
Static LLOQ can be used if no BQL flag column is mapped, but mapped columns override static values.
required_inputs: Selection of 'BQL?' checkbox in model options.
limitations: Log-likelihood calculations may overflow if censoring numbers are very small, particularly with multiplicative error models.
BQL handling is specific to Maximum Likelihood engines (e.g., Laplacian).
cards.downstream_use: Accurate parameter estimation in the presence of censored PK data. Avoiding bias from imputing BQL values as zero or LLOQ/2.

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
